items.title: Coordinate maps and permutations are measurable on finite products
items.statement:
Let $(S_i,\Sigma_i)$, $1\le i\le n$, be finitely many measurable spaces, with
$n\ge1$, and equip $\prod_{i=1}^nS_i$ with its finite product sigma-algebra.
If $f_i:(\Omega,\mathcal F)\to(S_i,\Sigma_i)$ are measurable, then the tuple
$f=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ is measurable. If all factors equal one measurable space
$(S,\Sigma)$, every coordinate permutation $\tau_\pi:S^n\to S^n$ is
measurable, where $(\tau_\pi z)_i=z_{\pi(i)}$.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, §§3.1 and 5.1

items.title: Regular conditional kernels push forward under measurable random maps
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ be a probability space, let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$, let $X$ be a random element of $(S,\Sigma)$, and let $K$ be a regular conditional distribution of $X$ given $\mathcal G$. If $T$ is a measurable space and $g:(\Omega,\mathcal G)\times(S,\Sigma)\to(T,\Tau)$ is measurable, then
$$K_g(\omega,B):=K\bigl(\omega,\{x:g(\omega,x)\in B\}\bigr),\qquad B\in\Tau,$$
is a regular conditional distribution of $g(\omega,X(\omega))$ given $\mathcal G$.

If, in addition, $U$ is a random element of a measurable space $(V,\mathcal V)$, is independent of $\mathcal G\vee\sigma(X)$, and has law $\lambda$, then $K(\omega,\cdot)\otimes\lambda$ is a regular conditional distribution of $(X,U)$ given $\mathcal G$.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, §§3.1, 5.1, 5.4–5.5

items.title: Exchangeable random elements
items.statement:
Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ be random elements, $n\ge1$, of one measurable space
$(\mathcal Z,\mathscr Z)$. Their tuple $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$ is a random element
of $(\mathcal Z^n,\mathscr Z^{\otimes n})$ by
[[lem-coordinate-maps-and-permutations-are-measurable-on-finite-products]],
and its law is the pushforward probability measure from
[[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]. For a permutation $\pi$ of
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\tau_\pi(z)_i=z_{\pi(i)}$. The tuple is
**exchangeable** if
$$\mathbb P_Z\circ\tau_\pi^{-1}=\mathbb P_Z\qquad\text{for every permutation }\pi.$$

This is invariance of the joint law, not an assertion of independence or identical marginal construction by independent sampling. The coordinate maps $\tau_\pi$ are measurable by the cited finite-product lemma.

references.title: Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §3.1
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §1

items.title: Conformal scores and rank p-values
items.statement:
Let $\mathcal Z=\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y$ be a feature-response measurable
space, let $m\ge0$, and put $n=m+1$. A **split score rule** is a jointly
measurable map $s:\mathcal H\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R$, where $H$ is a
training statistic with values in the specified measurable rule space
$(\mathcal H,\mathscr H)$. The measurable-statistic convention is that of
[[def-statistic-and-estimator]]. Once $H=h$ is fixed, calibration and test
scores are $R_i=s(h,Z_i)$; the rule does not change when it scores the
calibration or test example.

A **full score assignment** of length $n$ is a measurable map
$A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n):\mathcal Z^n\to\mathbb R^n$ that is
permutation-equivariant:
$$A(\tau_\pi z)=\tau_\pi A(z)\qquad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal Z^n\text{ and permutation }\pi.$$
For a candidate response $y$, append $(x,y)$ as the $n$th example and write
$R_i(y)=A_i(Z_1,\ldots,Z_m,(x,y))$ and $r=R_n(y)$.

For either a split score vector or a full augmented score vector, the
**nonrandomized upper-rank p-value** of the candidate is
$$p(y)=\frac1{m+1}\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}\mathbf1\{R_i(y)\ge R_{m+1}(y)\}.$$
An optional **tie-randomized rank p-value** is defined when a supplied random
variable $U$ has Lebesgue probability law on $[0,1]$ and is independent of the
data and training information:
$$p_U(y)=\frac{\#\{i\le m:R_i(y)>r\}+U\bigl(1+\#\{i\le m:R_i(y)=r\}\bigr)}{m+1}.$$
The added $1$ counts the candidate itself in its tie group. A single such $U$
is shared across a candidate scan. This is an explicit randomization; the
general Markov-kernel definition of a randomized procedure
[[def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel]] does not assert that arbitrary
kernels have a random-seed representation.

Here “uniform on $[0,1]$” means $\mathbb P(U\le u)=u$ for $0\le u\le1$.

Smaller scores are treated as more conforming. The rank formula counts all
ties conservatively in the nonrandomized version; the randomized formula
spreads the candidate uniformly over its entire tie block.

For a split candidate scan at a fixed feature value $x$, the notation in
these formulas is $R_i(y)=s(h,Z_i)$ for $1\le i\le m$ and
$R_n(y)=s(h,(x,y))$, with $r=R_n(y)$. Thus the calibration scores do not
depend on $y$, and the candidate is scored by the same fixed rule.

references.title: Jing Lei, Max G'Sell, Alessandro Rinaldo, Ryan J. Tibshirani, and Larry Wasserman, Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §§2.1–2.2 and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§3.1, 4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §§1–3

items.title: Finite order statistics and rank maps are measurable
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F)$ be a measurable space, let $R_1,\ldots,R_m$ be
measurable real-valued functions with $m\ge1$, and let $1\le k\le m$. The
$k$th order statistic $R_{(k)}$ is measurable. For a finite real score vector
$R_1,\ldots,R_n$ and another measurable real-valued function $U$ on the same
space, its upper-rank p-value and tie-randomized rank are measurable.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, §§3.1 and 5.1

items.title: Permutation-equivariant scores preserve exchangeability
items.statement:
Let $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)$ be an exchangeable random element of $\mathcal Z^n$,
and let $A:\mathcal Z^n\to\mathbb R^n$ be measurable and
permutation-equivariant in the sense of
[[def-conformal-nonconformity-score-and-rank-pvalue]]. Then $A(Z)$ is an
exchangeable real random vector.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.1 and Remark 2.4
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §3

items.title: Split conformal prediction set
items.statement:
Let $m\ge0$ calibration examples $Z_i=(X_i,Y_i)$ be scored by one fixed,
measurable score rule $s_H$ obtained from the training statistic $H$, and let
$0<\alpha<1$. Set
$$n=m+1,\qquad k=\lceil(m+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil.$$
Compute $R_i=s_H(Z_i)$ for $1\le i\le m$. Sort calibration observations by
the ordered keys $(R_i,i)$, so ties are broken by the fixed index order. If
$k\le m$, let $q$ be the score component of the $k$th ordered pair; if
$k=m+1$, set $q=+\infty$. For a feature value $x$, return
$$C(x)=\{y\in\mathcal Y:s_H(x,y)\le q\}.$$

The optional tie-randomized version uses one independent $U$ with Lebesgue
probability law on $[0,1]$, shared across the candidate scan, and returns
$$C_U(x)=\{y\in\mathcal Y:p_U(y)>\alpha\},$$
where $p_U$ is the score-rank formula in
[[def-conformal-nonconformity-score-and-rank-pvalue]]. The candidate score is
included in its tie group. The score maps must be jointly measurable in the
training, calibration, feature, and response variables; then membership in
each returned set is a measurable event by
[[lem-finite-order-statistic-and-rank-maps-are-measurable]].

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.2 and Appendix A.1
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §2

items.title: Full conformal prediction set
items.statement:
Let $m\ge0$ observed examples $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$ and $0<\alpha<1$ be given.
For each candidate $(x,y)$, append it to the examples and apply a measurable,
permutation-equivariant full score assignment of length $m+1$ from
[[def-conformal-nonconformity-score-and-rank-pvalue]], obtaining
$R_1(y),\ldots,R_{m+1}(y)$. Compute
$$p(y)=\frac1{m+1}\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}\mathbf1\{R_i(y)\ge R_{m+1}(y)\}$$
and return
$$C(x)=\{y\in\mathcal Y:p(y)>\alpha\}.$$

An optional exact-randomized version uses one independent $U$ with Lebesgue
probability law on $[0,1]$, shared across the candidate scan, and returns
$C_U(x)=\{y:p_U(y)>\alpha\}$. The full score map must be jointly measurable
in the observed examples, $x$, and $y$; the membership event is measurable by
[[lem-finite-order-statistic-and-rank-maps-are-measurable]].

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.1 and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §3

items.title: Conformal rank superuniformity under exchangeability
items.statement:
Let $R_1,\ldots,R_n$ be an exchangeable real random vector with $n\ge1$.
Define its last-coordinate upper-rank p-value by
$$p_n=\frac1n\#\{i\le n:R_i\ge R_n\}.$$
Then $\mathbb P(p_n\le u)\le u$ for every $u\in[0,1]$. If $U$ has Lebesgue
probability law on $[0,1]$ and is independent of $R$, define
$$p_{U,n}=\frac{\#\{i\le n:R_i>R_n\}+U\,\#\{i\le n:R_i=R_n\}}n.$$
Then $p_{U,n}$ has the uniform law on $[0,1]$.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.1 and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§3.1, 4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §§1–2

items.title: Split conformal marginal coverage
items.statement:
Let $Z_i=(X_i,Y_i)$, $1\le i\le m+1$, be random elements of one measurable
example space $(\mathcal Z,\mathscr Z)$, and let $\mathcal T$ be the training
sigma-field. Suppose the tuple $Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{m+1})$ has a regular
conditional distribution $Q_\omega$ given $\mathcal T$ in the sense of
[[def-regular-conditional-distribution]], whose sections have joint laws
invariant under every coordinate permutation, as in
[[def-exchangeable-random-elements]], for almost every $\omega$. Let $H$ be a $\mathcal T$-measurable
training statistic, and let $s:\mathcal H\times\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R$ be a
jointly measurable split score rule. Use the split set in
[[alg-split-conformal-prediction-set]] at $0<\alpha<1$. Then
$$\mathbb P\{Y_{m+1}\in C(X_{m+1})\mid\mathcal T\}\ge1-\alpha\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
If the tie-randomized set $C_U$ is used with one $U$ of Lebesgue probability
law on $[0,1]$ independent of $\mathcal T\vee\sigma(Z)$, then
$$\mathbb P\{Y_{m+1}\in C_U(X_{m+1})\mid\mathcal T\}=1-\alpha\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
In either case, integration over the training sigma-field gives the same
marginal lower bound or exact marginal coverage.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), Theorem 2.2 and Appendix A.1
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §2

items.title: Full conformal marginal coverage
items.statement:
Let $(\mathcal X,\mathscr X)$ and $(\mathcal Y,\mathscr Y)$ be measurable
feature and response spaces, let $m\ge0$, and let
$Z_i=(X_i,Y_i)$, $1\le i\le m+1$, be random elements of the product measurable
space $\mathcal Z=(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y,\mathscr X\otimes\mathscr Y)$.
Suppose their joint law is invariant under every coordinate permutation, as in
[[def-exchangeable-random-elements]]. Suppose a measurable, permutation-equivariant
full score assignment $A:\mathcal Z^{m+1}\to\mathbb R^{m+1}$ is used for every
augmented candidate sample, as in [[alg-full-conformal-prediction-set]]. Then,
for $0<\alpha<1$, its nonrandomized full conformal set satisfies
$$\mathbb P\{Y_{m+1}\in C(X_{m+1})\}\ge1-\alpha.$$
If the tie-randomized set uses one $U$ with Lebesgue probability law on
$[0,1]$, independent of $\sigma(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{m+1})$ and shared across the
candidate scan, then
$$\mathbb P\{Y_{m+1}\in C_U(X_{m+1})\}=1-\alpha.$$
These are marginal guarantees over the exchangeable examples and any stated
tie randomization.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), Theorem 2.1, Remark 2.4, and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §3

title: Conformal Prediction and Exchangeable Ranks — Examples

items.title: Split conformal coverage can be conservative when scores tie
items.statement:
Take a constant score rule $s(z)=0$, two calibration examples, one exchangeable
test example, and $\alpha=1/2$. All three scores are tied. The ordinary split
quantile set covers with probability $1$, while the specified independent
uniform tie-randomized rank set covers with probability exactly $1/2$.

items.title: Full conformal ranks a candidate in an augmented sample
items.statement:
Take feature space $\mathcal X=\{x_0\}$ and response space
$\mathcal Y=\{1,2,3\}$, each with its power-set sigma-algebra, so the product
example space is identified with $\mathcal Y$ by $(x_0,y)\mapsto y$. Let
$Z_1,Z_2,Z_3$ be a uniformly random ordering of the pairs
$(x_0,1),(x_0,2),(x_0,3)$, and use the response-coordinate score assignment
$A_i(z_1,z_2,z_3)=y_i$ when $z_i=(x_0,y_i)$. The true
candidate's nonrandomized upper-rank p-value is $1$, $2/3$, or $1/3$, each with
probability $1/3$. At $\alpha=0.4$, the full conformal set covers with
probability $2/3$.

items.title: Marginal split coverage need not give rare-subgroup coverage
items.statement:
Marginal split-conformal coverage at level $1-\alpha$ forces coverage at least
$1-\alpha$ conditional on every feature subgroup.

items.title: Exchangeability failure can destroy split coverage
items.statement:
The split-conformal lower coverage bound holds for arbitrary calibration and
test distributions, even when their joint law is not exchangeable.
